news.title: Preparing workers for the age of AI
news.summary_en: As artificial intelligence reshapes the workforce, the Brown School’s Jason Jabbari explains how higher education can prepare students with the skills to adapt and thrive while expanding economic opportunity.

news.title: New investments in humanities scholarship, academic inquiry
news.summary_en: Two new funding streams will examine how academic inquiry works and how collaboration bolsters the humanities.

news.title: Harnessing atomic structure to advance semiconductor technology
news.summary_en: McKelvey Engineering’s Rohan Mishra is helping to unlock the power of atomically thin materials to improve silicon-based transistors. The goal is to enable vastly more efficient electronic devices.

news.title: Callais’ impact on voting rights extends beyond 2026 midterms
news.summary_en: The 2026 midterm results may have softened the immediate political impact of the Supreme Court’s Louisiana v. Callais decision, but they don’t diminish its long-term consequences for voting rights and minority representation, says an election law expert at Washington University in St. Louis.

news.title: ‘Counterpublic 2026: Coyote Time’
news.summary_en: Counterpublic returns with “Coyote Time,” its third iteration. On view throughout the fall, the St. Louis-wide public art triennial — one of the largest in the United States — features more than 50 artists, including many associated with the WashU Sam Fox School.
